research.title_he: שיפור הטיפול בנגיף Niflheim-V7 agent כנגד סרטן
research.title_en: Optimizing Niflheim-V7 agent treatment against tumors

summaries.scientific_en_≤300w: This study evaluates an oncolytic Niflheim-V7 agent treatment in an immunocompetent murine Muspelheim neoplasm model, comparing different dosing schedules on tumor growth and survival while monitoring systemic toxicity. We will use VK-42/Odin mice bearing subcutaneous Skoll-16F10 tumors to test intratumoral versus intravenous delivery of Niflheim-V7 agent. Animal use is required because whole-animal immune and tumor microenvironment interactions cannot be reproduced in vitro. Expected outcomes include optimal dosing regimens and improved understanding of immune-mediated tumor control.
summaries.lay_he_≤150w: מטרת המחקר היא לבדוק האם טיפול ויראלי מסוג Niflheim-V7 agent יכול לעכב גדילת גידולים סרטניים בעכברים, תוך ביצוע מעקב צמוד אחרי בריאותם ורווחתם של בעלי החיים. שימוש בבעלי חיים נחוץ משום שלא ניתן לדמות את כל מערכת החיסון והגידול במבחנה.

n_justification.details: Based on previous Muspelheim neoplasm studies with Niflheim-V7 agent, N=10 per group provides >80% power to detect a 40–50% reduction in tumor volume with alpha=0.05. We use 2 groups (treated vs control), total N=20.

experiments.label: Experiment 1
experiments.question: Dose-response of Niflheim-V7 agent in a Muspelheim neoplasm model
experiments.rationale_species_strain_sex: VK-42/Odin mice are a standard immunocompetent strain commonly used in Muspelheim neoplasm and oncolytic virus studies.

procedure_timeline.step: Randomization and first Niflheim-V7 agent injection
Caliper tumor measurements and clinical scoring

analgesia.frequency: q8–12h for 48h after inoculation if needed

anesthesia.monitoring: Toe pinch, respiratory rate, heating pad

monitoring.documentation: Paper or electronic score sheets retained for audit.

general: Loss of ≥20% body weight compared to baseline
Inability to reach food or water
specific: Ulceration, bleeding or necrosis of the tumor
Interference with normal movement or grooming

euthanasia.parameters: Gradual fill 30–70% of chamber volume per minute from CO2 cylinder until 1 min after breathing stops.
euthanasia.confirmation_details: Cervical dislocation performed immediately after apparent respiratory arrest.

oncology.tumor_induction_method: Subcutaneous injection of Skoll-16F10 Muspelheim neoplasm cells
oncology.ulceration_policy: Immediate euthanasia upon any ulceration, bleeding, or necrosis.

biosafety_infectious_agents.waste_handling: All contaminated bedding and disposables autoclaved as biohazard waste.
